e-12694.knowledge_point: Negating a Sentence Containing a Conjunction
e-12694.problem:
What is the negation of the following compound statement? 

$\qquad$ $6$ is composite and $5\!\not{|} \, 3.$
e-12694.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
\neg ( A \land B) = \neg A \lor \neg B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(6\text{ is composite}\text{ and }5\,\text{⧸}|\,3) & ≡¬((6\text{ is composite})∧(5\,\text{⧸}|\,3)) \\  & ≡¬(6\text{ is composite})∨¬(5\,\text{⧸}|\,3) \\  & ≡(6\text{ is not composite})∨(5\,|\,3) \\  & ≡6\text{ is not composite}\text{ or }5\,|\,3.\end{aligned}
$$

e-12695.knowledge_point: Negating a Sentence Containing a Disjunction
e-12695.problem:
What is the negation of the following compound statement?

$\qquad$ $3$ is not prime or $\pi$ is not rational.
e-12695.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

$$
\neg ( A \lor B) = \neg A \land \neg B.
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(3\text{ is not prime}\text{ or }\pi \text{ is not rational}) & ≡¬((3\text{ is not prime})∨(\pi \text{ is not rational})) \\  & ≡¬(3\text{ is not prime})∧¬(\pi \text{ is not rational}) \\  & ≡(3\text{ is prime})∧(\pi \text{ is rational}) \\  & ≡3\text{ is prime}\text{ and }\pi \text{ is rational}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-12696.problem:
Simplify the statement $
eg ( (P \lor 
eg Q) \land (Q \lor 
eg P) )$ using De Morgan's laws.
e-12696.worked_solution:
De Morgan's laws state that

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∧Q)≡¬P∨¬Q, \\ ¬(P∨Q)≡¬P∧¬Q.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬((P∨¬Q)∧(Q∨¬P)) & ≡¬(P∨¬Q)∨¬(Q∨¬P) \\  & ≡(¬P∧¬(¬Q))∨(¬Q∧¬(¬P)) \\  & ≡(¬P∧Q)∨(¬Q∧P)\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
$\,$ $|{1,x}|\ne 0$ and $x$ is rational

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
after.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(|{1,x}|\ne 0\text{ and }x\text{ is rational}) & ≡¬((|{1,x}|\ne 0)∧(x\text{ is rational})) \\  & ≡¬(|{1,x}|\ne 0)∨¬(x\text{ is rational}) \\  & ≡(|{1,x}|=0)∨(x\text{ is not rational}) \\  & ≡|{1,x}|=0\text{ or }x\text{ is not rational}.\end{aligned}
$$

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B

Question 7
?

3|18 or 11 is not prime.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

a
3⧸|18 and 11 is prime
b
3|18 and 11 is prime
c
3⧸|18 or 11 is prime
d
3|18 and 11 is not prime
e
3|18 or 11 is prime
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B.

So, the negation of our statement is

¬(3|18 or 11 is not prime)≡¬((3|18)∨(11 is not prime))≡¬(3|18)∧¬(11 is not prime)≡(3⧸|18)∧(11 is prime)≡3⧸|18 and 11 is prime.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution declares option a: 3 does not divide 18 and 11 is prime. This agrees with De Morgan's law, which negates both parts and changes “or” to “and.”

Question 8
?

7=5 or −3≥0.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

a
7≠5 or −3>0
b
7≠5 and −3>0
c
7≠5 or −3≤0
d
7=5 and −3<0
e
7≠5 and −3<0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B

So, the negation of our statement is

¬(7=5 or −3≥0)≡¬((7=5)∨(−3≥0))≡¬(7=5)∧¬(−3≥0)≡(7≠5)∧(−3<0)≡7≠5 and −3<0.

content.problem:
$\,$ $7=5$ or $-3\ge 0.$

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
content.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

$$
¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(7=5\text{ or }-3\ge 0) & ≡¬((7=5)∨(-3\ge 0)) \\  & ≡¬(7=5)∧¬(-3\ge 0) \\  & ≡(7\ne 5)∧(-3<0) \\  & ≡7\ne 5\text{ and }-3<0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:

$$
¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(2\text{ is not prime}\text{ or }2\notin Q) & ≡¬((2\text{ is not prime})∨(2\notin Q)) \\  & ≡¬(2\text{ is not prime})∧¬(2\notin Q) \\  & ≡(2\text{ is prime})∧(2\in Q) \\  & ≡2\text{ is prime}\text{ and }2\in Q.\end{aligned}

Question 9
?

2 is not prime or 2∉Q.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?

a
 2 is prime or 2∉Q
b
 2 is prime and 2∈Q
c
 2 is not prime or 2∈Q
d
 2 is not prime and 2∈Q
e
 2 is prime or 2∈Q
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B

So, the negation of our statement is

¬(2 is not prime or 2∉Q)≡¬((2 is not prime)∨(2∉Q))≡¬(2 is not prime)∧¬(2∉Q)≡(2 is prime)∧(2∈Q)≡2 is prime and 2∈Q.

EXPLANATION

De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B.

So, the negation of our statement is ¬(−1 is not negative or {−1} is not empty)≡¬((−1 is not negative)∨({−1} is not empty))≡¬(−1 is not negative)∧¬({−1} is not empty)≡(−1 is negative)∧({−1} is empty)≡−1 is negative and {−1} is empty.

¬(P∧Q)≡¬P∨¬Q,¬(P∨Q)≡¬P∧¬Q.

¬((¬P∧¬Q)∨(P∧¬Q))≡¬(¬P∧¬Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q)≡(¬(¬P)∨¬(¬Q))∧(¬P∨¬(¬Q))≡(P∨Q)∧(¬P∨Q)

$$
